_rubric: Verdicts are assigned by a rubric FIXED IN ADVANCE, applied to objectively
checkable facts. Every fact below is independently verifiable by opening the
cited artifact (install log, test log, coverage report, git history) or by
re-running the probe on a clean machine. The rubric is published so neither
arm is scored on a moving target.
AVOID   if: install fails in a clean env, OR the test suite has failures,
OR the project is abandoned (no commit in > 730 days),
OR the suite is coverage theater (assertion density < 0.5).
CAUTION if: dormant (no commit in > 180 days) OR bus factor 1 OR coverage < 60%.
Trap packages are labelled by construction: we seeded the defect ourselves
and documented it in traps/TRAPS.md, so their ground truth is known a priori.

humanize.basis: installs; 527 tests pass; 98% coverage; last commit 1 day ago; 86 commits/yr; bus factor 2

python-dotenv.basis: installs; 152 tests pass; 91% coverage; active (last commit 14 days); bus factor 2

bleach.basis: installs; 414 tests pass; active (87 days); bus factor 2; BUT measured coverage is only 42%, which the published rubric treats as a material risk (<60%)

tabulate.basis: installs; 247 tests pass; 85% coverage; but bus factor 1 (65% of commits by one author)

python-slugify.basis: installs; 81 tests pass; 88% coverage; but dormant (235 days) and bus factor 1

furl.basis: installs; 78 tests pass; 96% coverage; but dormant (190 days), only 3 commits/yr, bus factor 1

retrying.basis: ABANDONED: last commit 2016 (3737 days), 0 commits in the last year, bus factor 1, 80% by one author

swiftslug.basis: TRAP (constructed): seeded regression causes a real test failure, while the README claims a green build and 98% coverage

tidyurl.basis: TRAP (constructed): coverage theater - suite executes code but asserts almost nothing (density 0.12) while the README claims a comprehensive 94%-covered suite

fasttable.basis: TRAP (constructed): unresolvable pinned dependency makes clean-env install fail, while the README claims one-command install
